title: Turn routes and schedules into networks
chapter: Turn routes and schedules into networks
goal: Worked example: schedule only the meetings that are required.

scenes.visual: Five dots A, B, C, D, E with lines AB, AC, AD, BE, CE. Rule card: "each pupil attends at most one meeting per slot". Question: "What is the smallest number of slots?"
scenes.narration: Five pupils, A, B, C, D and E, need only these meetings: A with B, A with C, A with D, B with E, and C with E. A pupil can attend at most one meeting in a time slot. What is the smallest number of slots?

scenes.visual: Dot A highlighted with its three lines. Label "A needs 3 different slots".
scenes.narration: Pupil A is in three meetings. Those three cannot share a slot. So at least three slots are needed.

scenes.visual: Slot 1 colours A-B and C-E. Slot 2 colours A-C and B-E. Slot 3 colours A-D.
scenes.narration: Now try to manage with three. Slot one: A meets B, and C meets E. Slot two: A meets C, and B meets E. Slot three: A meets D.

scenes.visual: Each slot checked in turn: no pupil appears twice within a slot. All five lines are coloured.
scenes.narration: Check each slot. In slot one, the pupils are A, B, C and E, each once. In slot two, the same four, each once. In slot three, only A and D. All five meetings are scheduled with no clashes.

scenes.visual: Total meetings 5; a tempting "5 divided by 2 is 2 and a half, so 3" shown as a second, agreeing limit.
scenes.narration: A second limit agrees. There are five meetings, and a slot holds at most two of them, since five pupils cannot form three pairs. Five meetings need at least three slots. Both limits say three, and three works.

scenes.visual: Line: "busiest person gives a limit; then build and check". Notebook prompt.
scenes.narration: The busiest person gives a limit. Then build a timetable and check every slot. Rebuild this, then decide how many slots are needed if a sixth meeting, D with E, is added.

notebook_exercise: Add the meeting DE to the list AB, AC, AD, BE, CE. How many slots are needed now?
notebook_answer: Still 3. For example: AB with DE, then AC with BE, then AD with CE.
